You must require the full codes with all files, in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code.

The technical description itself is missing from your message, so I cannot rewrite it faithfully yet. A strong build prompt works best when it is structured around explicit instructions, clear constraints, project structure, testing expectations, and the relevant source context rather than guessed details.[1][2]

## What to send

Paste the full technical description exactly as you want it transformed. If it is long, include everything in one block and preserve headings, file lists, APIs, data models, workflows, constraints, dependencies, edge cases, and acceptance criteria, because specification quality depends heavily on complete context and well-structured requirements.[2][1]

## What I will return

I will convert it into one single prompt that is strictly technical, sequential, and implementation-focused, with no role-play language, no conversational filler, no references to the original software name, and no fake or placeholder content. I will also make the prompt explicit about architecture, file-by-file deliverables, commands, testing, boundaries, and production-ready completeness, because those are core elements of effective AI coding specs.[1]

## Paste-ready format

Use this format in your next message so I can rewrite it immediately:

```text
TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION
<<<
[paste the complete technical description here]
>>>

OPTIONAL CONSTRAINTS
<<<
- target stack:
- required languages/frameworks:
- deployment environment:
- database:
- authentication:
- third-party integrations:
- performance/security requirements:
- output format preferences:
>>>
```

## Master prompt shell

If you want, you can also use this neutral prompt shell now and replace the technical description block with your actual source text:

```text
Rewrite the following technical description into a single, comprehensive implementation prompt.

Requirements for the rewritten prompt:

- Write as a complete build specification from beginning to end.
- Describe step by step exactly what will be constructed and exactly how it will be constructed.
- Keep the wording strictly technical, objective, explicit, and unambiguous.
- Do not include role-playing, persona framing, motivational language, or polite filler.
- Do not mention or reveal the name of any original software product, application, service, or codebase even if the source description is clearly about re-implementing one.
- Preserve all real technical requirements, architecture details, workflows, interfaces, constraints, edge cases, and acceptance criteria from the source description.
- Expand vague statements into precise implementation instructions where the intent is clear from the source.
- Do not omit hard parts, shortcuts, or non-happy-path behavior.
- Do not allow simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, stubbed, or fake content, logic, APIs, services, datasets, or UI elements.
- Require complete, production-ready output with full code for every file needed to build and run the system.
- Require real implementations for backend, frontend, database, infrastructure, authentication, validation, error handling, state management, logging, testing, and deployment whenever those are relevant to the source description.
- Require all files in full, with no abridgement.
- Require explicit project structure with every file path included.
- Require installation, setup, migration, seed, build, test, and run commands where applicable.
- Require environment variable definitions and configuration files where applicable.
- Require database schemas, models, migrations, and seed logic where applicable.
- Require API contracts, request/response schemas, validation rules, and error responses where applicable.
- Require UI flows, component behavior, loading states, empty states, error states, and accessibility behavior where applicable.
- Require security controls, permission boundaries, and input sanitization where applicable.
- Require unit, integration, end-to-end, and smoke tests where applicable.
- Require the final output to be internally consistent across all files and commands.
- Do not output explanations about the rewrite process.
- Output only the final rewritten prompt.

Source technical description:
<<<
[PASTE SOURCE DESCRIPTION HERE]
>>>
```

Send the actual technical description, and I will turn it into the final single prompt.
